title: Definition
body_md:
Let $ {\cal R} $ be a unitary fusion category. The tube category associated with
    $ {\cal R} $, denoted by $\mathsf{Tube}_{\mathrm v}( {\cal R} )$, is a unitary linear category defined by
    the following data.
    \begin{itemize}
        \item[-] The objects of $\mathsf{Tube}_{\mathrm v}( {\cal R} )$ are the objects of $ {\cal R} $;
        \item[-] For $A,B\in {\cal R} $, the morphism space in $\mathsf{Tube}_{\mathrm v}( {\cal R} )$ is
        defined by
        \[
        \mathsf{Tube}_{\mathrm v}( {\cal R} )(A, B) := \bigoplus_{i\in\mathrm{Irr} {\cal R} } {\cal R} (A\otimes i, i\otimes B).
        \]
        That is, any morphism $u$ in $\mathsf{Tube}_{\mathrm v}( {\cal R} )(A,B)$ is an
        $\mathrm{Irr} {\cal R} $-graded vector of the form
        \[
        \left(\raisebox{-28.65274pt}{\includegraphics{figures/tikz/tube-morphism-component.pdf}}\right)_{i\in\mathrm{Irr} {\cal R} },
        \]
        where each $u_i$ is a morphism in $ {\cal R} (A\otimes i, i\otimes B)$;
        \item[-] For $u\in \mathsf{Tube}_{\mathrm v}( {\cal R} )(B,C)$ and
        $v\in \mathsf{Tube}_{\mathrm v}( {\cal R} )(A,B)$, their composition is defined by
        \[
        (u\circ v)_k = \sum_{i,j\in\mathrm{Irr} {\cal R} }\sum_{\alpha = 1}^{N^{ji}_k}
        \raisebox{-57.10547pt}{\includegraphics{figures/tikz/tube-morphism-composition.pdf}}.
        \]
        Here
        \[
            \left\{q_\alpha\in  {\cal R} (k, j\otimes i): \alpha = 1,2,\ldots, N^{ji}_k\right\}
        \]
        is an orthonormal basis of $ {\cal R} (k, j\otimes i)$;
        \item[-] The dagger structure~\cite{Green_2024} is defined by
        \[
        \left(\raisebox{-28.65274pt}{\includegraphics{figures/tikz/tube-morphism-before-adjoint.pdf}}\right)^\dagger :=
    \raisebox{-28.65274pt}{\includegraphics{figures/tikz/tube-morphism-after-adjoint.pdf}}.
        \]
    \end{itemize}

name: Vertical tube category

label: eq:anyon-insertion-rep
title: Definition
body_md:
For $x=(X,\gamma_{X,-})$ and $A \in  {\cal R} $, define $x^\sharp(A):= {\cal R} (X,A)$. For
$A,B\in {\cal R} $, define the action of $x^\sharp$ on tube morphisms by the linear
map
\begin{equation}\label{eq:anyon-insertion-rep}
    x^\sharp_{A,B}:\mathsf{Tube}_{\mathrm v}( {\cal R} )(A,B)
    \rightarrow\mathsf{Hilb}\bigl( {\cal R} (X,A), {\cal R} (X,B)\bigr)
\end{equation}
determined as follows. For $V\in {\cal R} $ and
$u:A\otimes V\rightarrow V\otimes B$, its action on
$\phi:X\rightarrow A$ is defined algebraically by~\cite{Lan_2014,Green_2024}
\begin{equation}\label{eq:anyon-insertion-partial-trace}
    x^\sharp_{A,B}\left(\pi_V^{A,B}(u)\right)(\phi)
    :=\operatorname{ptr}^{\ell}_V\!\left[
        u\circ(\phi\otimes\mathrm{id}_V)\circ\gamma_{X,V}^{-1}
    \right].
\end{equation}
This action is graphically represented by
\[
\raisebox{-52.21042pt}{\includegraphics{figures/tikz/central-object-action.pdf}}.
\]
Equation~\eqref{eq:anyon-insertion-partial-trace} uses the inverse half-braiding to move the
$V$-string across the $X$-string.
We call $x^\sharp$ the \emph{anyon-insertion representation functor}, associated with $x$.

title: Proof
body_md:
By Proposition~\ref{prop:hardiman-tube-center-equivalence}, the
anyon-insertion functors $z^\sharp$, with $z\in\mathrm{Irr}\mathfrak{Z}( {\cal R} )$, form a complete
set of simple tube representations. The semisimple Yoneda
decomposition of the tube category then gives Eq.~\eqref{eq:tube-sector-decomposition}.
Under this isomorphism, composition and the dagger operation act
componentwise.

label: rem:hardiman-numerics
title: Remark
body_md:
The half-braiding construction for resolving topological sectors was
implemented numerically for the non-braided Haagerup fusion category
$\mathcal H_3$ in Ref.~\cite{Vanhove_2022}. An alternative procedure using
central idempotents of the MPO tube algebra was applied to
strange-correlator transfer matrices in Ref.~\cite{Bal_2018}, building on
Ref.~\cite{Bultinck_2017}. Here we formulate the anyon-insertion construction
as the $*$-functor $x^\sharp:\mathsf{Tube}_{\mathrm v}( {\cal R} )\to\mathsf{Hilb}$, establish the sector
decomposition of general tube morphisms, and apply it to transfer morphisms
produced by Loop-TNR.
\label{rem:hardiman-numerics}
head: environment
name: Relation to previous sector-resolution methods

label: rem:defect-line-tnr
title: Remark
body_md:
Hauru et al.~\cite{Hauru_2016} extracted sector-resolved conformal spectra
using symmetry defects and charge resolution. For $ {\cal R} =\mathsf{Rep}(\mathbb{Z}_n)$, the
defect and charge labels $(g,\chi)$ correspond to the simple objects of
$\mathfrak{Z}(\mathsf{Rep}(\mathbb{Z}_n))$. The present construction extends this description to
fusion-category symmetries. The anyon is inserted when constructing the
transfer morphism, so the same renormalized tensors can be used to resolve
all sectors. We do not follow the RG flow of a lattice defect operator,
such as the Kramers--Wannier duality operator.
\label{rem:defect-line-tnr}
head: environment
name: Relation to defect-line TNR

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $u \in \mathsf{Tube}_{\mathrm v}( {\cal R} )(A, A)$ be a morphism. For each
    $x\in\mathrm{Irr}\mathfrak{Z}( {\cal R} )$, define the sector partition function by
    \[
    Z_x(u):=\mathrm{Tr}_{x^\sharp(A)}\left[x^\sharp_{A,A}(u)\right].
    \]
    The partition vector of $u$ is the vector indexed by $\mathrm{Irr}\mathfrak{Z}( {\cal R} )$,
    \[
    Z(u):=\left(Z_x(u)\right)_{x\in\mathrm{Irr}\mathfrak{Z}( {\cal R} )}.
    \]
    Equivalently, $Z(u)$ is obtained by applying the ordinary trace
    componentwise to the sector decomposition $\Phi_{A,A}(u)$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Using the basis $I=(i,\alpha,\beta)$ from
Eq.~\eqref{eq:forget-embedding}, it suffices to consider simple objects
$A=a$ and $B=b$.  Regarding both sides as morphisms in $\mathsf{Tube}_{\mathrm h}( {\cal R} )$ and taking
the weighted direct sum $\bigoplus_a d_a/D_ {\cal R} ^2$, the desired identity becomes
\begin{multline}
\bigoplus_a\frac{d_a}{D_ {\cal R} ^2}\sum_\alpha\frac{1}{D_ {\cal R} ^2}
\sum_{y}\frac{S_{xy}}{d_Y} \\
\times \raisebox{-28.65274pt}{\includegraphics{figures/tikz/modular-s-sum-over-y.pdf}} \\
    =\frac{1}{D_ {\cal R} ^2}
\raisebox{-30.95274pt}{\includegraphics{figures/tikz/modular-s-center-loop.pdf}}.
\end{multline}

By Proposition~\ref{prop:hardiman-tube-center-equivalence}, the
anyon-insertion representations jointly detect morphisms in $\mathsf{Tube}_{\mathrm h}( {\cal R} )$.
For $z=(Z,\gamma_{Z,-})\in\mathrm{Irr}\mathfrak{Z}( {\cal R} )$, both sides act on
\[
\raisebox{-28.75273pt}{\includegraphics{figures/tikz/modular-s-z-sector.pdf}},
\]
as
\[
\frac{1}{D_ {\cal R} ^2}\frac{S_{xz}}{d_Z}\times
\raisebox{-28.75273pt}{\includegraphics{figures/tikz/modular-s-z-sector-weight.pdf}}.
\]
Here we have used the graphical center projector of
Lemma~3.10 of Ref.~\cite{mueger2001subfactorscategoriestopologyii}:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:center-projector}
    \raisebox{-28.85274pt}{\includegraphics{figures/tikz/center-projector-input.pdf}}\mapsto
\sum_{i\in\mathrm{Irr} {\cal R} }\frac{d_i}{D_ {\cal R} ^2}
\raisebox{-30.95274pt}{\includegraphics{figures/tikz/center-projector-output.pdf}}.
\end{equation}
It projects $ {\cal R} (X,Y)$ onto
$\mathfrak{Z}( {\cal R} )\bigl((X,\gamma_{X,-}),(Y,\gamma_{Y,-})\bigr)$.

label: def:stable-symto
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:stable-symto}
Let $ {\cal T} $ be a (1+1)d CFT realized as a boundary theory of the symTO
$\mathfrak{Z}( {\cal R} )$. We call $\mathfrak{Z}( {\cal R} )$ a \emph{stable symTO for $ {\cal T} $} if, apart
from the identity operator, the trivial bulk-anyon sector of $ {\cal T} $ contains
no relevant local operator. Equivalently, it contains no nonidentity
local operator with scaling dimension $\Delta<2$.

label: prop:diagonal-algebra
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:diagonal-algebra}
    Let $ {\cal C} $ be a unitary fusion category, and let $ {\cal C} ^{\mathrm{rev}}$
    denote the category with reversed tensor product,
    $X \otimes^{\mathrm{rev}} Y := Y \otimes X$. Set
    \[
        A := \bigoplus_{i\in\mathrm{Irr}( {\cal C} )} i^* \boxtimes i,
        \qquad D := \sqrt{\sum_{i\in\mathrm{Irr}( {\cal C} )} d_i^2}.
    \]
    Let $q^A_{i^*\boxtimes i}\colon i^*\boxtimes i\to A$ be the
    orthonormal summand embeddings. For each $i,j,k\in\mathrm{Irr}( {\cal C} )$, choose
    an orthonormal basis
    $\{q^{i\otimes j}_{k,\alpha}\}_{\alpha=1}^{N^{ij}_k}$ of
    $ {\cal C} (k,i\otimes j)$. Define $m\colon A\otimes A\to A$ by
\begin{align}
	&\left(q^A_{k^*\boxtimes k}\right)^\dagger\circ m\circ
    \left(q^A_{i^*\boxtimes i}\otimes q^A_{j^*\boxtimes j}\right) \nonumber\\
	&\quad := \frac{1}{D}\sqrt{\frac{d_id_j}{d_k}} \sum_{\alpha}\left(q^{i \otimes j}_{k,\alpha}\right)^*\boxtimes \left(q^{i\otimes j}_{k,\alpha}\right)^\dagger \nonumber\\
	&\quad = \frac{1}{D}\sqrt{\frac{d_id_j}{d_k}}\sum_{\alpha}
    \raisebox{-20.11682pt}{\includegraphics{figures/tikz/diagonal-algebra-fusion-left.pdf}}
    \boxtimes
    \raisebox{-20.11682pt}{\includegraphics{figures/tikz/diagonal-algebra-fusion-right.pdf}}.
\end{align}
    Here $*$ denotes the dual morphism, $\dagger$ denotes the adjoint,
    and the dotted arrows indicate the tensor-product directions. In particular,
    \[
    \left(q^{i \otimes j}_{k,\alpha}\right)^*
    :=
    \raisebox{-20.11682pt}{\includegraphics{figures/tikz/diagonal-algebra-multiplication.pdf}}.
    \]
    Define the unit $\iota\colon\mathbb{1}\boxtimes\mathbb{1}\to A$ by
    \[
        \iota := D\,q^A_{\mathbb{1}^*\boxtimes\mathbb{1}}.
    \]
    Then $(A,m,\iota)$ is a Q-system in $ {\cal C} ^{\mathrm{rev}}\boxtimes {\cal C} $,
    with normalization
    \[
        m\circ m^\dagger=\mathrm{id}_A,
        \qquad \iota^\dagger\circ\iota=D^2\,\mathrm{id}_{\mathbb{1}\boxtimes\mathbb{1}}.
    \]
head: environment
name: Canonical (Longo--Rehren) Q-system

title: Proof
body_md:
A unitary change of fusion basis acts on the dual and adjoint factors
    by mutually conjugate matrices, so the sum defining $m$ is unchanged and therefore $m$ is well-defined.

    We depict $m$ and $m^\dagger$ by black trivalent vertices, and
    $\iota$ and $\iota^\dagger$ by white univalent vertices. In the
    Q-system relations below, all strands carry $A$ and compositions
    are read from top to bottom.

    Associativity is the graphical identity
    \[
        \raisebox{-18pt}{\includegraphics{figures/tikz/qsystem-associativity-left.pdf}}
        =
        \raisebox{-18pt}{\includegraphics{figures/tikz/qsystem-associativity-right.pdf}}.
    \]
    To verify it, fix the external labels $i,j,k,l$.
    Both compositions of $m$ have the same normalization factor
    $D^{-2}\sqrt{d_id_jd_k/d_l}$. Keeping this factor explicit,
    the paired recoupling gives
    \begin{align*}
        &\frac{1}{D^2}\sqrt{\frac{d_id_jd_k}{d_l}}
        \sum_{e,\alpha,\beta}
        \raisebox{-29pt}{\includegraphics{figures/tikz/qsystem-f-left-dual-p.pdf}}
        \boxtimes
        \raisebox{-29pt}{\includegraphics{figures/tikz/qsystem-f-left-adjoint-p.pdf}}
        \\
        &\quad =\frac{1}{D^2}\sqrt{\frac{d_id_jd_k}{d_l}}
        \sum_{f,\gamma,\delta}\sum_{g,\rho,\sigma}
        \\*
        &\qquad\times\Biggl[
        \sum_{e,\alpha,\beta}
        F^{ijk}_{l,(f,\gamma,\delta),(e,\alpha,\beta)}
        \overline{F^{ijk}_{l,(g,\rho,\sigma),(e,\alpha,\beta)}}
        \Biggr]
        \\*
        &\qquad\times
        \raisebox{-29pt}{\includegraphics{figures/tikz/qsystem-f-right-dual-q.pdf}}
        \boxtimes
        \raisebox{-29pt}{\includegraphics{figures/tikz/qsystem-f-right-adjoint-r.pdf}}
        \\
        &\quad =\frac{1}{D^2}\sqrt{\frac{d_id_jd_k}{d_l}}
        \sum_{f,\gamma,\delta}
        \raisebox{-29pt}{\includegraphics{figures/tikz/qsystem-f-right-dual-q.pdf}}
        \boxtimes
        \raisebox{-29pt}{\includegraphics{figures/tikz/qsystem-f-right-adjoint-q.pdf}}.
    \end{align*}
    As in the multiplication diagram, reversed strand arrows and the
    dotted tensor-product direction indicate the dual factor. Duality
    preserves the recoupling coefficient, while taking the adjoint
    complex conjugates it. The last equality follows from unitarity
    \[
    \begin{aligned}
        &\sum_{e,\alpha,\beta}
        F^{ijk}_{l,(f,\gamma,\delta),(e,\alpha,\beta)}
        \overline{F^{ijk}_{l,(g,\rho,\sigma),(e,\alpha,\beta)}}\\
        &\qquad=\delta_{fg}\,\delta_{\gamma\rho}\,\delta_{\delta\sigma}.
    \end{aligned}
    \]
    Thus the intermediate object and both multiplicity labels agree
    in the two factors, proving associativity.

    When either input is the tensor unit, the coefficient in $m$ is $D^{-1}$.
    The factor $D$ in $\iota$ therefore gives both unit laws
    \[
        \raisebox{-14.42636pt}{\includegraphics{figures/tikz/frobenius-unit-insertion-left.pdf}}
        =
        \raisebox{-14.42636pt}{\includegraphics{figures/tikz/frobenius-unit-insertion-right.pdf}}
        =
        \raisebox{-14.42636pt}{\includegraphics{figures/tikz/frobenius-unit-reduced-strand.pdf}}.
    \]

    Orthogonality of the fusion bases gives, on the $k^*\boxtimes k$ summand,
    \[
        \left.m\circ m^\dagger\right|_{k^*\boxtimes k}
        =\frac{1}{D^2}\sum_{i,j}N^{ij}_k\frac{d_id_j}{d_k}
        \,\mathrm{id}_{k^*\boxtimes k}
        =\mathrm{id}_{k^*\boxtimes k}.
    \]
    The last equality uses
    $\sum_j N^{ij}_k d_j=d_i d_k$, which follows from rigidity and
    multiplicativity of quantum dimensions. The normalization of $\iota$
    follows from its definition, and $d_A=\sum_i d_i^2=D^2$.
    Graphically, these normalization conditions are
    \[
        \raisebox{-21.53955pt}{\includegraphics{figures/tikz/frobenius-bubble-removal.pdf}}
        =
        \raisebox{-21.53955pt}{\includegraphics{figures/tikz/frobenius-identity-strand.pdf}},
        \qquad
        \raisebox{-16pt}{\includegraphics{figures/tikz/qsystem-unit-norm.pdf}}
        =D^2.
    \]

    In a $C^*$ tensor category, unitality, associativity, and
    $m\circ m^\dagger=\mathrm{id}_A$ imply the Frobenius relations
    \[
    \begin{aligned}
        (m\otimes\mathrm{id}_A)\circ(\mathrm{id}_A\otimes m^\dagger)
        &=m^\dagger\circ m,\\
        (\mathrm{id}_A\otimes m)\circ(m^\dagger\otimes\mathrm{id}_A)
        &=m^\dagger\circ m.
    \end{aligned}
    \]
    The two Frobenius relations are represented by
    \[
        \raisebox{-21.53955pt}{\includegraphics{figures/tikz/frobenius-left-associated-tree.pdf}}
        =
        \raisebox{-21.53955pt}{\includegraphics{figures/tikz/frobenius-associativity-tree.pdf}}
        =
        \raisebox{-21.53955pt}{\includegraphics{figures/tikz/frobenius-right-associated-tree.pdf}}.
    \]
    Thus $(A,m,\iota)$ satisfies the Q-system relations in the normalization
    used in Sec.~\ref{sec:random-cluster-models}. In particular, $m^\dagger$
    is an $A$-bimodule section of $m$, so $A$ is separable.

label: prop:diagonal-condensable
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:diagonal-condensable}
    Let $ {\cal C} $ be a unitary braided fusion category with braiding $\beta$.
    Equip $ {\cal C} ^{\mathrm{rev}}$ with the braiding
    \[
        \beta^-_{X,Y}\colon
        X\otimes^{\mathrm{rev}}Y=Y\otimes X
        \xrightarrow{\beta_{X,Y}^{-1}}
        X\otimes Y=Y\otimes^{\mathrm{rev}}X.
    \]
    Then the canonical Q-system $A$ of
    Proposition~\ref{prop:diagonal-algebra} is a condensable algebra,
    namely a connected commutative separable algebra, in
    $( {\cal C} ^{\mathrm{rev}},\beta^-)\boxtimes {\cal C} $.
    Under the braided equivalence
    \[
        ( {\cal C} ^{\mathrm{rev}},\beta^-)\cong\overline{ {\cal C} },
        \qquad \overline\beta_{X,Y}:=\beta_{Y,X}^{-1},
    \]
    it defines a condensable algebra in $\overline{ {\cal C} }\boxtimes {\cal C} $.
    If $ {\cal C} $ is a UMTC, this algebra is Lagrangian.

label: def:injective-gapless-boundary
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:injective-gapless-boundary}
A boundary $(\mathscr{V},{}^{\mathrm{Mod}_\mathscr{V}}\! {\cal S} )$ of $ {\cal C} $ is \emph{injective} if
\[
     {\cal C} \cong(\mathrm{Mod}_\mathscr{V})_{\mathscr{A}}^{\mathrm{loc}},
    \qquad  {\cal S} \cong(\mathrm{Mod}_\mathscr{V})_{\mathscr{A}}
\]
for a condensable algebra $\mathscr{A}\in\mathrm{Mod}_\mathscr{V}$.

label: def:stable-full-field-algebra
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:stable-full-field-algebra}
The algebra $\mathscr{B}$ is \emph{stable} if
$\operatorname{Rel}(\mathscr{B})=0$. When $\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathscr{B}}$ has the required
braided vertex tensor structure, we call the symTO $\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathscr{B}}$ stable
if $\mathscr{B}$ is stable.
